subject: Azure private offer — packaging tiers, discount harmonization, and partner margin
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@calyxhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Peterson <jill.peterson@calyxhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — packaging tiers, discount harmonization, and partner margin

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the call earlier. We ran the draft PO by procurement overnight and they came back with two asks before we can approve: a) can you confirm a clean SKU mapping for the committed tiers (we need a clear migration path from dev -> prod SKUs), and b) evidence of the partner/reseller margin carveout for BrightPath (they're insisting on an 18% net margin minimum).

I've attached the draft PO (Calyx_Azure_PO_Draft_v3.pdf) and a short note from procurement. Our priority is to keep list-price discounts aligned across regions; procurement is nervous about ad-hoc rebate language.

Can you put together a succinct packaging proposal that shows: committed SKU names, effective list price, discount bands by commit, and the resulting partner pass-through/net margin? If you can share a simple workback table, that would help accelerate approval.

Proposed timeline: final PO signed by next Friday (10/30) if we can lock margins and SKU mapping this week.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Chen
Head of Cloud Procurement
Calyx Health
alex.chen@calyxhealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@calyxhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — packaging tiers, discount harmonization, and partner margin

Alex — really appreciate the clear asks. Attaching a concise workback (partner_margin_workback.xlsx) and a suggested SKU mapping below. I kept it conservative so procurement has room to approve without changing downstream partner math.

Quick summary (proposal):
- Packaging: Dev (dev-1 / 4 vCPU equiv) -> Staging (stg-1) -> Prod (prod-1 / reserved GPU pools)
- Commit bands: 0-10k, 10k-50k, 50k+ (monthly Azure consumption USD).
- List price baseline: $0.12/token equivalent for prod SKU, staged discounts at 12% / 18% / 25% respectively.
- Partner carve: suggest an 18% net margin floor for BrightPath, implemented as a fixed pass-through percentage on Redwood net revenue.
- Overage protection: capped overage credit for first quarter after go-live (to ease transition).

Requests from our side: please confirm BrightPath's legal entity and billing flow (direct-bill vs. pass-through). If BrightPath requires invoiced commissions, we'll need partner agreement addendum.

Next steps:
1) Naomi — can you validate the overage cap language and confirm the legal/finance hooks for partner margin evidence?
2) Alex/Jill — can you confirm partner billing expectation and if procurement needs a templated partner carve clause?

If that looks good I can produce a one-page amendment for the private offer that we can attach to the PO.

Best,
Rishi

On Wed, Oct 20, 2026 at 11:03 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — really appreciate the clear asks. Attaching a concise workback (partner_margin_workback.xlsx) and a suggested SKU mapping below.

Hi Alex / Rishi — tagging in Finance & RevOps notes here. I reviewed the proposed bands and have three practical edits that make the private offer approvable from our side while protecting partner economics: 

1) Partner margin carve: we can formalize an 18% floor as a pass-through percentage of Redwood net revenue, but it needs an audit/evidence clause. Recommend: quarterly evidence package (invoicing + simple reconciliation) for the first two quarters.
2) Overages / credits: keep Rishi's capped overage credit, but define a clear trigger: credits apply only if usage exceeds committed band by >25% month-over-month and only for one billing cycle.
3) List price parity: procurement's ask about regional alignment is valid. We'll include a clause that prevents retroactive unilateral list-price changes impacting the committed term (requires 60-day notice and mutual consent for changes that would worsen net partner economics).

Legal/finance boilerplate I'm proposing (draft language):
"Partner Margin Evidence: Within 30 days of quarter close, Redwood will provide BrightPath and Calyx Health with a reconciliation report showing Redwood net revenue attributable to the private offer, and the partner pass-through calculation establishing the 18% floor. Parties may request supporting invoices; Redwood will provide redacted copies limited to transaction ID, SKU, quantity, and net amount."

Camila — can you slot a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the workback and we can thread in partner ops to confirm billing flow?

Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@calyxhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Azure private offer — packaging tiers, discount harmonization, and partner margin

Thanks all — that language works for procurement, and BrightPath confirmed they're happy with the 18% floor plus the quarterly evidence package. BrightPath will accept the overage protection as defined.

We're comfortable to move forward on the following:
- Redwood to produce one-page private offer amendment (SKU mapping + commit bands + partner margin clause).
- Calyx to circulate final PO to legal for signature once amendment attached.

I'll upload a signed MSA stub to the Drive (attached here as Calyx_signed_MSA_stub.pdf) and loop BrightPath legal in the next note. Can Rishi share the one-page amendment by EOD tomorrow so procurement can review?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this is time-sensitive for our migration window.

Best,
Alex
